claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The forward deployed engineer playbook is defined as an operating manual for embedding engineers inside customer environments to discover, prototype, deploy, and feed learnings back into the core product.
claims.quote: A forward deployed engineer playbook is the operating manual for a function that embeds engineers inside customer environments to discover problems, prototype solutions, deploy them, and feed the learnings back into the core product.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Palantir originated the model, and its dual Echo/Delta team structure reportedly helped drive a 640% return on its embedded approach.
claims.quote: The model originated at Palantir — whose dual Echo/Delta team structure helped drive a reported 640% return on its embedded approach — and is now standard at Anthropic, OpenAI, Scale AI, and most Series A AI startups.

claims.quote: and is now standard at Anthropic, OpenAI, Scale AI, and most Series A AI startups.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: FDE functions differ from professional services because services are measured on billable hours and bespoke delivery, while FDEs are measured on what returns to the product.
claims.quote: This is the structural difference from professional services. A services team is measured on billable hours and bespoke delivery; an FDE function is measured on what comes back to the product.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: The FDE engagement lifecycle has five phases with owners, deliverables, gates, and a 30-60-90-120 structure.
claims.quote: The FDE engagement lifecycle runs through five distinct phases, each with an owner, a deliverable, and a gate that must clear before the next phase starts. Run it as a 30-60-90-120 structure with explicit exit criteria; skipping a gate is how engagements drift into open-ended consulting.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: By day 90, an engagement must produce at least one generalized feature merged into the core product.
claims.quote: The deliverable is a merged, generalized capability in the core product. The gate, by day 90: at least one productized feature traceable to this engagement.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Teams under pressure skip discovery and prototype before mapping the real problem, building the wrong thing fast; week-1/week-4/week-12 interviews are meant to prevent this.
claims.quote: Teams under pressure jump to prototyping before mapping the real problem, then build the wrong thing fast. The week-1/week-4/week-12 interview cadence exists to prevent this.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: Handoff includes documentation, coaching the customer's internal team, and transferring the relationship to customer success and product engineering, typically within 120 days of go-live.
claims.quote: The FDE writes comprehensive documentation, coaches the customer's internal DevOps or data engineering team on maintaining and scaling the system, and hands the relationship to customer success and product engineering — typically within 120 days of go-live.
